title: Pasting of canonical truncation and cohomology comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with bounded t-structures [def-weil-t-structure]. For each exact functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserving both halves at all integer cutoffs and equipped with coherent shift comparisons $c^j_{F,N}:F(N[j])\simeq(FN)[j]$, let $\alpha^-_{F,j},\alpha^+_{F,j}$ be its canonical truncation comparisons characterized by the counit and unit equations [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison]. Put $\mathcal H^j=(\tau^{\ge j}\tau^{\le j})[j]$, with values in the heart, and set $N=\tau^{\ge j}\tau^{\le j}K$. The formula
$$q_{F,j,K}=\bigl(\tau^{\ge j}(\alpha^-_{F,j,K})\circ\alpha^+_{F,j,\tau^{\le j}K}\bigr)[j]\circ c^j_{F,N}$$
defines a natural isomorphism $F\mathcal H^j\simeq\mathcal H^jF$ for every integer $j$.

For another such functor $G$ and a natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ commuting with the shift comparisons, one has
$$q_{G,j,K}\circ\eta_{\mathcal H^jK}=\mathcal H^j(\eta_K)\circ q_{F,j,K}.$$
For a third bounded t-category $\mathcal B$ and an exact t-exact functor $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$, with the composite shift comparisons on $HF$, one has
$$q_{HF,j,K}=q_{H,j,FK}\circ H(q_{F,j,K}),\qquad q_{\mathrm{id},j,K}=1.$$
Consequently let $U:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$, $V:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ and $F':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D'$ be exact t-exact functors of bounded t-categories, all with shift comparisons, and let $b:VF\simeq F'U$ commute with shifts. For either canonical truncation $\tau=\tau^{\le m}$ or $\tau^{\ge m}$ and for cohomology the following squares commute (subscripts distinguish the category only when necessary):
$$\alpha_{F',UK}\circ F'(\alpha_{U,K})\circ b_{\tau K}=\tau(b_K)\circ\alpha_{V,FK}\circ V(\alpha_{F,K}),$$
$$q_{F',j,UK}\circ F'(q_{U,j,K})\circ b_{\mathcal H^jK}=\mathcal H^j(b_K)\circ q_{V,j,FK}\circ V(q_{F,j,K}).$$
These squares respect identity comparisons and pasting of successive such squares, including specified shift-compatible associators.

proof.text: Use the existing Mathlib lower- and upper-bound instances for truncGELE j j in TruncLEGT. Thus the double truncation has both bounds j. TStructure.isLE_shift and isGE_shift put its j-shift in degree zero. Apply mem_heart_iff. Functor.IsTExact.isLE_obj and isGE_obj preserve these bounds under F, proving the three heart assertions. This uses only the t-structure infrastructure [def-weil-t-structure], not the homological-functor or short-exact-triangle theorem.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3, 1.3.5 and Theorem 1.3.6, printed pp. 29–31; translation of the heart construction to cutoff j

proof.text:
Write $a_{F,K}=\alpha^-_{F,j,K}$ and $d_{F,K}=\alpha^+_{F,j,K}$, and define only as an abbreviation within this proof
$$A_{F,K}=R_{\mathcal D}(a_{F,K})\circ d_{F,L_{\mathcal C}K}:F(T_{\mathcal C}K)\longrightarrow T_{\mathcal D}(FK).$$
Both factors are natural isomorphisms by [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison]. For $f:K\to K'$, their naturality equations give $T_{\mathcal D}(Ff)A_{F,K}=A_{F,K'}F(T_{\mathcal C}f)$ by substitution. Shifting this equation and using naturality of $c_F^j$ gives naturality of $q_{F,j,K}=A_{F,K}[j]\circ c^j_{F,T_{\mathcal C}K}$. Each factor is invertible, so this is the asserted natural isomorphism. This is exactly the formula in the statement, with its specified order of the two truncations.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), printed pp. 29–30; agent composition of the two given natural truncation isomorphisms with the assumed shift comparison
Proposition 1.3.3(i), printed pp. 29–30; agent substitution of the existing transformation equations and the assumed shift-compatibility equation

proof.text:
For composable $F,H$, the composition clause of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] gives $a_{HF,K}=a_{H,FK}H(a_{F,K})$ and $d_{HF,L_{\mathcal C}K}=d_{H,F L_{\mathcal C}K}H(d_{F,L_{\mathcal C}K})$. Substitute these into $A_{HF,K}$ to obtain
$$R_{\mathcal B}(a_{H,FK})R_{\mathcal B}(H(a_{F,K}))d_{H,F L_{\mathcal C}K}H(d_{F,L_{\mathcal C}K}).$$
Naturality of the already given comparison $d_H$ on the arrow $a_{F,K}:F L_{\mathcal C}K\to L_{\mathcal D}FK$ says
$$R_{\mathcal B}(H(a_{F,K}))d_{H,F L_{\mathcal C}K}=d_{H,L_{\mathcal D}FK}H(R_{\mathcal D}(a_{F,K})).$$
Replacing these adjacent factors and combining the two $H$-images proves $A_{HF,K}=A_{H,FK}H(A_{F,K})$. The identity clause of the same cited statement gives $A_{\mathrm{id},K}=1$. These are calculations with the given comparisons, not extra comparison lemmas.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), printed pp. 29–30; agent expansion of the existing composition and identity laws

proof.text:
Put $N=T_{\mathcal C}K$ and $M=T_{\mathcal D}FK$. By definition of composite shift comparisons,
$$c^j_{HF,N}=c^j_{H,FN}H(c^j_{F,N}).$$
Naturality of $c_H^j$ at the arrow $A_{F,K}:FN\to M$ is
$$H(A_{F,K})[j]c^j_{H,FN}=c^j_{H,M}H(A_{F,K}[j]).$$
Insert the formula for $A_{HF}$ from step 4 into $q_{HF}=A_{HF}[j]c^j_{HF,N}$ and use this naturality equation. This yields
$$q_{HF,j,K}=A_{H,FK}[j]c^j_{H,M}H(A_{F,K}[j])H(c^j_{F,N})=q_{H,j,FK}H(q_{F,j,K}).$$
For the identity functor, equipped as usual with its identity shift comparisons, step 4 gives $q_{\mathrm{id},j,K}=1[j]\circ1=1$. The only comparison input to this substitution is the composition and identity clause of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison].

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), printed pp. 29–30; agent calculation using naturality and the assumed composite shift comparisons

proof.text: Apply the transformation clause of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] to $b:VF\Rightarrow F'U$. It gives $\alpha_{F'U,K}b_{\tau K}=\tau(b_K)\alpha_{VF,K}$, for each of the two truncations separately. Its composition clause identifies the left comparison with $\alpha_{F',UK}F'(\alpha_{U,K})$ and the right comparison with $\alpha_{V,FK}V(\alpha_{F,K})$. Substitution proves the stated truncation square. For cohomology, step 3 applied to the same shift-compatible $b$ gives $q_{F'U,j,K}b_{\mathcal H^jK}=\mathcal H^j(b_K)q_{VF,j,K}$. Substitute step 5 for each composite comparison. This is precisely the displayed cohomology square. All composite functors here preserve both halves, since each constituent does.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3(i), printed pp. 29–30; agent substitution of transformation and composition equations for the square b

proof.text: Construct the pasted isomorphism e : F ⋙ (V ⋙ W) ≅ (U ⋙ S) ⋙ F'' by the specified associators, whiskering b by W, and whiskering d by U. The standard CommShift instances prove its shift compatibility. Apply the already proved square theorem directly to e, U ⋙ S, and V ⋙ W. Expand the two composite truncation comparisons using the composition clause of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison], and expand the cohomology comparisons using step 5. Expand the components of e and the whiskerings, then use functoriality and associativity to obtain exactly the three displayed horizontal pasting equations. Iteration gives finite pasting.

source.place: Agent pasting calculation from the equations in steps 2–6; categorical composition and naturality only

proof.text:
Identity transformations give identity squares by substituting $b=1$ in step 6; identity outer functors can be removed by the identity comparison laws of [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] and step 5. For vertical composition of transformations $b:E\Rightarrow E'$ and $d:E'\Rightarrow E''$, the two equations give
$$r_{E''}(db)_P=r_{E''}d_Pb_P=P(d)r_{E'}b_P=P(d)P(b)r_E=P(db)r_E.$$
Finally a specified shift-compatible associator $a:E\simeq E'$ between two parenthesizations is itself a transformation to which the truncation transformation clause and step 3 apply: $r_{E',K}a_{PK}=P(a_K)r_{E,K}$. Thus inserting an associator changes a comparison by exactly these two boundary components; it preserves every square. For successive associators $a,a'$, the equation just computed for $a'a$ agrees with the equations for $a$ and $a'$ composed. This verifies the asserted compatibility with the specified associators without identifying parenthesized functors silently.

source.place: Agent identity, transformation-composition and associator calculation from Proposition 1.3.3(i) and steps 3–7

proof_origin.place: BBD Proposition 1.3.3(i)-(ii) and Theorem 1.3.6, pp. 29-31. G7 formalization: Mathlib bounds on double truncation and shifts give heart membership directly; the existing canonical truncation-comparison laws give transformation, identity and composition. Horizontal pasting applies the square theorem to the explicitly associated and whiskered pasted isomorphism. Vertical pasting applies naturality to the composite transformation.
